scenes.title: Seeds for the Island
scenes.narration: Bea arrived at the harbour with a sealed orange box of seeds. The island garden needed them for its spring opening. The morning sea was calm, and a marked stone path was beginning to appear as the tide fell. "The box must stay dry. These seeds have travelled a long way." She kept the box under her coat and went to the harbour office.

scenes.title: Two Ways Across
scenes.narration: Jon showed Bea the harbour map. The marked path would be open for another hour. The supply boat would leave in twenty minutes and return from the island later that morning. Both routes reached the garden before opening time. "The path gives you a quiet walk. The boat carries tools as well." Bea thanked him and checked that the orange box was still sealed.

scenes.title: The Keeper’s Request
scenes.narration: The garden keeper called the office radio. She had space ready for the seeds and needed a spare watering can. Bea could take the marked path now, or wait with Jon and carry the can on the boat. "Either way, the seeds will arrive. I must choose how to help." Outside, the sea remained calm. The orange box was light enough for either journey.
scenes.prompt: What extra item does the keeper ask for?
scenes.explanation: The keeper asks for a spare watering can in addition to the seeds.

scenes.title: A Garden Before the Crowd
scenes.narration: Bea followed the marked stone path and reached the garden while the keeper was arranging empty pots. Together, they put the orange box on a dry workbench. Jon would bring the watering can on the boat. "I have time to help you prepare the first row." They planted the seeds before the visitors arrived. Looking back across the calm water, Bea could see the blue boat leaving the harbour.

scenes.title: An Extra Pair of Hands
scenes.narration: Bea waited with Jon, then travelled on the supply boat. She kept the orange box on her lap while Jon secured the watering can beside the tools. At the island, the keeper met them at the small landing. "We brought your watering can, and the seeds are still dry." Together, they carried everything into the garden. Bea stayed to help the keeper welcome the first visitors, glad that one journey had carried two kinds of help.
